en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape that is clearly visible from many miles away.
Inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River, visitors can observe massive limestone stalactites and stalagmites hanging from the cave ceiling.
Taal Lake in Batangas completely surrounds Volcano Island, creating a visible lake inside an island inside a larger lake.
Farmers carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the Ifugao mountains, creating giant visible steps for cultivating rice.
The rare Rafflesia plant found in Philippine rainforests produces the largest observable individual flower in the world.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
During the wet season, dark cumulonimbus clouds visibly gather over the Philippine seas, bringing heavy afternoon thunderstorms.
The Philippine tarsier possesses enormous observable eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it see at night.
Giant oysters in Palawan open to reveal the South Sea pearl, a large, highly visible natural gemstone.
The Hundred Islands National Park in Pangasinan features observable karst limestone formations resembling scattered green hills during high tide.
Mangrove forests in Olango Island feature visible above-ground roots that trap coastal sediment and provide safe nurseries for young fish.
Mount Pinatubo's crater now holds a visible, deep blue crater lake formed after its massive 1991 eruption.
